output.name: Ommen
output.myth: When the string was cut, the drowned went aloft by sea, and the sea would not give them back. Kael casts for them and never catches one, so Ommen was made to carry the names. Say a name at the harbour mouth on the drowning night and it is lit, one lantern each, and the boat sails out along the Leeward Reach with its lamps trailing on a rope. Tavo came down cold that year, tore the sails, and laughed, but the boat went on, because Hesk had counted every name and would not lose one. Halvet, the other lantern boat, lies north-east, and her three women and a boy went up the same night. Halesk, the Stilled Gull, hangs off to the south-west with her neck stretched up for rain. My mother's brother is up there, third lamp from the stern. In hard southern weather, look for the mast. If it is lit, someone is being remembered. If it is dark, go down and say a name so the boat has something to carry.
output.finding: Start at Halvet, the Lantern Boat, and look a hand-span and a fist (about 28°) to her south-west to find Ommen.
